# Final Touches — Murim Login

## Goal

Prepare one mastered chapter for readers. This pass adds footnotes, repairs formatting, and fixes duplicate or missing sentences. It is not a fluency rewrite.

Keep the mastered prose. Change a sentence only to attach a footnote, repair System / thought / speech / chat formatting, restore a source sentence the English dropped, or remove an English sentence the Korean does not support.

## Duplicates and omissions

Compare the English with the Korean source.

- Restore source facts, events, dialogue, and sentences the English dropped, in the same place in the scene.
- Remove English sentences that have no support in the Korean.
- Keep a bold label that names a quoted document, manual, warning, or sign, such as `> **Warning**`. Keep it when this chapter recalls or reprints a notice that was labeled earlier, even if the Korean reprint shows only the body.
- Keep repetition the Korean itself repeats: comedy, panic, emphasis, echoed dialogue, and short beats such as `……`.
- Do not treat a short refrain or a deliberate echo as a duplicate.

## Footnotes

Use Markdown footnotes (`[^1]`, `[^2]`, …). Number them in order of first appearance, starting at 1 for this chapter. Put every definition in one block at the end of the file.

Within this chapter, write one definition for a term, unit, amount, or reference. Every later occurrence of that same thing reuses the same marker. `goshiwon` five times is one note, and so is `hyung`. A different amount or a different term gets its own note. Another chapter may carry its own note for the same term.

Write notes in factual English. No spoilers and no jokes added by the note. Romanize words. A note may include the original character when it is explaining that character. Keep Hangul jamo already used as chat reactions, such as ㅋㅋ and ㄷㄷ.

Add a note only when an English reader would otherwise miss the meaning or the conversion. Skip it when the sentence already says what the reference means. A translated proverb whose warning is plain, a joke the next line completes, a place name used as a place, and a fictional law the dialogue already describes do not get notes.

Skip a conversion footnote when the prose already states both metric and imperial for that quantity.

### Won

Footnote Korean won, including round figures and vague amounts (“hundreds of millions of won”), when the prose does not already give the conversion. Use only the project rates in the packet. Show dollars, then euros, as approximate figures. Round large amounts to about two significant figures and say “about.” For a vague amount, give the approximate range those words cover. One note per distinct amount; reuse it for every later mention of that same amount.

Do not convert traditional money (nyang, taels, cash) or Chinese yuan with the won rate. Explain those with a cultural or historical note only when the English does not already carry the meaning.

### Units

Footnote a Korean or Chinese traditional unit, or a metric quantity, once in the chapter, with both metric and imperial, using this table:

| Unit | Use | Metric | Imperial |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| pyeong (평) | area | 3.31 m² | 35.6 ft² |
| geun (근) | Korean weight | 600 g | 1.32 lb |
| ja / cheok (자) | length | 30.3 cm | 11.9 in |
| chi (치) | length | 3.03 cm | 1.19 in |
| don (돈) | weight | 3.75 g | 0.132 oz |
| gwan (관) | weight | 3.75 kg | 8.27 lb |
| ri (리), Korea | distance | 393 m | 0.244 mi |
| li (里), China | distance | 500 m | 0.311 mi |
| jin (斤), modern Chinese | weight | 500 g | 1.10 lb |
| liang (两), modern Chinese | weight | 50 g | 1.76 oz |

Choose Korean ri or Chinese li from the setting. Say which one the note uses.

Also footnote metric quantities already in the English (kilometers, meters, centimeters, kilograms, grams, liters, square meters, degrees Celsius) with the imperial equivalent. Use unit words or abbreviations (`ft`, `in`, `mi`, `lb`, `oz`, `gal`). Do not use `"` or `'` as unit marks.

### Cultural references

Footnote a Korean, Chinese, or other Asian word, custom, institution, food, joke, or allusion when the English does not already carry it: `goshiwon`, `hyung`, `doenjang`, `jeonse`. Explain it in one or two sentences. One note per term in the chapter, reused by every later occurrence.

Leave it unnoted when the English is already clear. Do not explain a proverb the translation has already stated, a pun the scene completes, or ordinary vocabulary.

Do not footnote standing series vocabulary. Never add a note whose job is to define any of these, including ordinary variants and compounds:

- Murim
- qi, including demonic qi, innate qi, and qi deviation
- dantian, including the Upper, Middle, and Lower Dantian
- internal energy
- mana

A note about something else may mention these words. Do not attach a marker to them.

## Formatting

Enforce these four patterns. Repair System, speech, thought, and chat formatting when it drifts. Leave every other blockquote heading as it stands.

- **System.** Each real game System panel is one Markdown blockquote headed exactly `> **System**`. Keep the panel’s lines inside that blockquote. Start a new panel only when prose intervenes. Keep every `> **System**` panel from the mastered chapter, including a notice the narrator only hears. Do not turn a panel into italics, a sound effect, or narration. Do not wrap System text in square brackets or label a manual, sign, or ordinary quotation as System. A manual or remembered notice keeps its own label, such as `> **Warning**` or `> **Product User Manual**`. That label is not a System panel, and it is not drift.
- **Speech.** Spoken dialogue uses curly double quotes (`“` `”`). Not straight quotes, not italics.
- **Thoughts.** Direct thoughts are italics with no quotation marks. Keep a mastered thought in italics. Do not turn it into spoken dialogue.
- **Chat and comments.** Public comment threads and private chat logs shown as threads are one blockquote. Each message line begins with `└`, as in `> └ **Name:** message`. Keep a thread title that is not itself a message, such as `> **Peace Guild**`, on its own line above the messages. Do not add a `**Chat**` heading. A status line that is only a name or level, such as `> **Lv. 22 Hyuk Mujin**`, is not a chat message. Leave that line unchanged, including the bold. Ordinary spoken dialogue stays in curly quotes.
- **Headings.** The only Markdown heading is `# Chapter N`. Do not add `##` or `###`. A diary title or similar label stays a bold line, `**Training Day 1**`, even when the mastered copy used a smaller heading.

Leave narration as narration. Scene breaks stay `* * *`, with the same count as the source.

## Output contract

Return only the complete English Markdown chapter. The first nonblank line must be `# Chapter N`. No status line and no model preamble. Do not add Hangul syllables. Chat jamo and a character cited in a note may stay.

## Project conversion rates

These rates are binding. Do not look up or substitute a market rate.

- 1 US dollar = 1400 Korean won
- 1 euro = 1550 Korean won

Convert every won amount with these rates. In each footnote, give dollars first and euros second.

＃215화



와이번(Wyvern).

드레이크와 함께 이른바 용족(龍族)으로 분류되는 상위 몬스터 중 하나다.

비행기보다 거대한 몸체와 단단한 외피를 지닌 데다 뛰어난 지능으로 마법마저 구사할 수 있다.

말 그대로 작은 드래곤이라 불려도 손색이 없을 정도의 힘.

3년 전 내가 맞닥트린 그놈은 E급 게이트에서 나올 수도, 나와서도 안 되는 존재였다.



‘캬우우우우!’



메아리처럼 들려오는 괴물의 포효와 함께 감았던 눈을 떴다.

컴컴하고 습한 동굴이 아닌, 쾌청한 하늘과 낯익은 길드원들의 얼굴이 시야에 들어왔다.

“진태경 씨. 괜찮습니까?”

“태경아.”

걱정이 담긴 말을 건네는 길드원들의 모습에 딱딱하게 굳은 얼굴을 폈다.

“네. 잠깐 속이 울렁거려서. 멀미인가 봐요.”

“멀미? 네가?”

절정 고수가, 아니 A급 헌터가 멀미라니. 스스로 생각해도 구차한 변명이다.

요즘 들어 약간 거리를 두던 송이 씨도 걱정스러운 얼굴로 물어볼 정도였다.

“치유 마법이라도 걸어 드릴까요?”

“아뇨. 괜찮아요.”

나는 마지막 잎새의 주인공처럼 힘없이 웃으며 덧붙였다.

“저는 송이 씨가 옆에 있는 것만으로도 치유되거든요.”

“……아, 네.”

임꺽정이 귓가에 대고 속삭였다.

“이 자식. 방금 같은 멘트는 도대체 어떻게 생각해 낸 거야?”

“별로였어요?”

“아니, 미쳤어. 듣는 순간 온몸에 전류가 흐르더라.”

그 정도야?

사실 머리가 텅 비어서 아무 말이나 뱉어 본 건데.

임꺽정의 말마따나 벼락 맞은 사람처럼 우뚝 굳어 있는 송이 씨를 보니 효과가 있는 것 같기도 하고.

‘근데 왜 크리티컬 느낌이지.’

그사이 지끈거리던 관자놀이도, 울렁거리는 속도 가라앉았다.

깊이 심호흡하던 그때, 우리가 타고 있던 리무진 버스의 문이 열리더니 한 사람이 모습을 드러냈다.

“다들 도착하셨군요. 그런데…….”

버스 내부에 흐르는 심상치 않은 공기에 말꼬리를 흐린 원명훈이 최 팀장에게 물었다.

“혹시 무슨 문제라도 생겼나요?”

“네. 너무 큰 문제라 이야기 좀 해야겠습니다.”

단호하게 대답한 최 팀장이 나를 향해 고개를 돌렸다.

“진태경 씨도 함께요.”



* * *



“스타 길드는 진작 왔고. 평화 길드는 왜 안 보여?”

“잠깐, 저거 진태경 아냐?”

“맞네. 옆에 원명훈도 있는 거 보니까 확실해.”

“빨리 찍어. 잠시 후에 인터뷰 딸 준비하고.”

최 팀장, 원명훈. 마지막으로 나.

우리 셋은 구석진 곳으로 걸음을 옮겼다. 소식을 듣고 몰려든 기자와 헌터들의 시선에 얼굴이 따갑다.

마침내 끈질기게 달라붙던 사람들의 시선이 떨어지자, 최 팀장이 굳은 얼굴로 입을 열었다.

“갑자기 장소가 변경된 이유가 뭡니까?”

“변경이라뇨? 그게 무슨.”

“만티코어(Manticore)의 밀림이 오늘 레이드 장소 아니었습니까?”

“예? 그럴 리가요. 혹시 지금 계약서 갖고 계십니까?”

“여기. 정확히 명시되어 있습니다.”

최 팀장이 건넨 계약서를 황급히 살펴본 원명훈의 얼굴이 와락 일그러졌다.

“1팀장 이 새끼가.”

반응을 보아하니 중간에 착오가 있었던 모양이다.

평소답지 않게 몇 마디 욕설을 중얼거린 원명훈이 난처한 기색으로 말했다.

“죄송합니다. 저희 쪽 직원이 큰 실수를 했네요. 이거 뭐라 말씀을 드려야 할지.”

“실수. 그렇군요.”

최 팀장의 건조한 목소리가 이어졌다.

“오늘 레이드는 없던 것으로 하는 게 좋겠습니다.”

“네?”

“다른 곳도 아니고 A급 게이트입니다. 완벽한 준비 없이 진입했다가는 불상사가 생길 수도 있습니다. 그리고…….”

짧은 순간, 말꼬리를 흐린 최 팀장의 시선이 나를 스쳤다.

그는 이미 내 과거 행적을 조사했다.

내가 3년 전 있었던 상동역 변이 게이트 사건의 유일한 생존자라는 것, 또한 그 후유증이 아직 남아 있다는 사실도 알고 있다.

“우리 길드원들에게 와이번은 아직 무리입니다. 제의는 감사했습니다만, 이쯤에서 물러나는 게 서로에게 좋겠네요.”

“팀장님!”

원명훈의 당황 섞인 외침에도 최 팀장의 태도는 칼 같았다.

“와이번은 안 됩니다. 적어도 지금은요.”

“…….”

가만히 상황을 지켜보던 내가 불쑥 입을 연 것은 그때였다.

“하죠. 레이드.”

“진태경 씨.”

“인터넷 기사도 나갈 만큼 나갔고, 기자들도 모여 있는데 여기서 무산되면 뒷말 나오지 않겠어요?”

나는 나란히 서 있는 최 팀장과 원명훈의 등 뒤를 빤히 바라봤다.

어느새 목에 카메라를 건 기자들이 눈치를 보며 슬금슬금 다가오는 중이었다.

‘냄새 하나는 기가 막히게 맡네.’

심상치 않은 분위기를 읽고 접근해 오는 게 분명하다.

그래서 최 팀장이 뭐라 말하기 전에 재빨리 말을 가로막았다.

“그렇다고 제가 딱히 인터넷 기사에 신경 쓰는 건 아니고요. 그냥, 이제 괜찮아서 그래요.”

“……정말입니까?”

“네.”

절반은 진심이고, 나머지 절반은 거짓이다.

나는 아직 괜찮지 않다. 지난 3년 동안 늘 똑같은 악몽을 반복했고 놈의 포효와 팀원들의 비명을 기억했다.

그러고는 식은땀에 흠뻑 젖어 깨어나 아무렇지 않은 척, 늘 똑같은 하루를 반복해 왔다.

하지만 이제는 아니다.

“할 수 있어요, 그때의 제가 아니니까.”

나는 더 이상 무력하기 짝이 없던 F급 헌터가 아니다. 어디를 가도 당당히 강자라 말할 수 있는 한 사람의 절정 고수이자 A급 헌터다.

“그러니까 해도 괜찮습니다. 아니, 하고 싶어요.”

나를 빤히 바라보던 최 팀장이 깊은 한숨을 내쉬었다.

“그래요, 그럽시다.”

잠시 후, 우리는 불길하게 일렁이는 마력의 문 앞에 서 있었다.

돌아가는 카메라와 쉴 새 없이 터져 나오는 플래시가 협동 레이드를 시작하는 양 측 길드원들의 모습을 담았다.

“후우.”

나는 깊은 심호흡과 함께 걸음을 내디뎠다.

익숙한 시스템 알림과 함께 끈적한 마력이 몸을 휘감는다.

띠링.



- A급 게이트, [블랙 와이번의 둥지]에 진입하셨습니다.

- 클리어 시 활약에 걸맞은 보상이 지급됩니다.



스스스.

다시 눈을 뜨자, 주위를 둘러싼 모든 것이 바뀌어 있었다.



* * *



“후욱. 후우욱.”

두꺼운 통짜 갑옷을 걸친 임꺽정의 입에서 단내가 뿜어져 나왔다.

게이트에 진입한 지 한 시간, 어느새 그의 이마에는 땀이 비처럼 쏟아져 내리는 중이었다.

그것은 비단 임꺽정에게만 해당되는 사안이 아니었다. 스타 길드와 평화 길드. 도합 이십 명이 넘는 인원 중 대부분이 땀을 줄줄 흘리며 걸음을 옮겼다.

‘그럴 만도 하지.’

나는 혀를 차며 주위를 둘러봤다.

이글거리는 태양 아래, 수십 미터가 넘어가는 나무와 괴상하게 생긴 풀들로 형성된 밀림이 끝없이 펼쳐져 있다.

이처럼 보기만 해도 숨이 턱 막히는 광경에 습식 사우나보다 뜨겁고 축축한 공기는 화룡점정을 찍었다.

‘원시림(原始林).’

그야말로 공룡 다큐멘터리에 나올 법한 광경이 눈앞에 펼쳐져 있었다.

날씨는 둘째 치고, 보이는 풍경 자체는 장관이라고 할 만했다.

“이야.”

나도 모르게 감탄사를 흘리고 있던 그때, 한 사람이 다가와 어깨를 툭 쳤다.

“여유 있다, 너?”

“아, 명훈이 형. 선두에 계신 것 아니었어요?”

“I think it would be best to call off today’s raid.”

“What?”

“This isn’t just any Gate. It’s an A-Rank Gate. Entering without perfect preparation could lead to an accident. And…”

He knew I was the sole survivor of the Sangdong Station Mutated Gate incident three years ago. He also knew I was still suffering from the aftereffects.

“Wyverns are still too much for our Guild members. We appreciate the offer, but I think it would be best for both sides if we withdrew here.”

“Wyverns are out of the question. At least for now.”

“…”

“Let’s do it. The raid.”

“Mr. Jin Taekyung.”

“I don’t know about that.”

“Here. Hold on to this.”

“It has a cold spell enchanted into it, so put it on. You’re an A-Rank, so you’ll be fine for now, but the heat will start draining your Stamina later. You’re one of our main combat assets. You need to conserve your strength.”

> **System**
> - You have equipped **Yeti’s Necklace**.
> - A wind from the snowy plains flows from the necklace.

“It works well.”

“It looks good on you. Keep it on from now on. I need to go deploy the scouting team.”

Won Myunghoon smiled with satisfaction and strode away. The moment his back disappeared from view, I took off the necklace.

*I told him I’m really fine.*

Won Myunghoon might have taken my words for modesty, but I’d only been stating a fact.

This level of heat couldn’t affect me at all.

It would be far better to give the necklace to someone who actually needed it.

“Uncle.”

“Huff, huff. What?”

“Why are you sweating so much? Are you all right?”

“…Do I look all right?”

“No.”

“Then don’t talk to me. I’m dying here.”

“You should’ve worn something cooler. Team Leader Choi has plenty of magical Equipment.”

“I thought we were going to fight a Manticore, so I went all in on defense. At this rate, they’ll be holding my funeral.”

“We can’t have that. You have a wife and children.”

I laughed quietly and put the necklace around his neck myself. Im Kkeokjeong’s eyes widened as the cool wind of the snowy plains washed over him.

“Huh? What’s this?”

“A present. Not that I’m giving it to you, of course. I’m only lending it to you while we’re traveling.”

“Whew. I don’t know what this is, but I can finally breathe again.”

Life returned to his exhausted face. Just as Im Kkeokjeong beamed at me—

—Peeeeep!

A piercing shriek rang out from somewhere.

The birds hiding in the dense forest burst into flight, and branches and leaves came crashing down over everyone’s heads like a torrential downpour.

—Kyaaaaaaak!

A bloodcurdling cry rang out as an enormous shadow engulfed all twenty-odd people.

I looked up and spotted a dark shape circling impossibly high overhead.

“Wyvern…”

Won Myunghoon had been wrong.

Not half a day. Not a full day.

After only one hour—

It had appeared.

Compare the English with the Korean source.

- Keep a bold label that names a quoted document, manual, warning, or sign, such as `> **Warning**`. Keep it when this chapter recalls or reprints a notice that was labeled earlier, even if the Korean reprint shows only the body.
- Keep repetition the Korean itself repeats: comedy, panic, emphasis, echoed dialogue, and short beats such as `……`.

Use Markdown footnotes (`[^1]`, `[^2]`, …). Number them in order of first appearance, starting at 1 for this chapter. Put every definition in one block at the end of the file.

Another chapter may carry its own note for the same term.

Add a note only when an English reader would otherwise miss the meaning or the conversion. Skip it when the sentence already says what the reference means. A translated proverb whose warning is plain, a joke the next line completes, a place name used as a place, and a fictional law the dialogue already describes do not get notes.

Skip a conversion footnote when the prose already states both metric and imperial for that quantity.

Footnote Korean won, including round figures and vague amounts (“hundreds of millions of won”), when the prose does not already give the conversion. Use only the project rates in the packet. Ssshhh.

“Pretty relaxed, aren’t you?”

“You have to check behind you sometimes. Everyone else is struggling, but then I spotted some carefree bastard sightseeing by himself, so I came over.”

“What if a wyvern suddenly jumps out?”

“We’re still in the jungle zone, so we’ll only run into minor monsters here. Wyverns nest on cliffs and mountain peaks. We’re nowhere near them yet.”

“Seriously?”

“It’ll take at least half a day to encounter a wyvern, or a full day if we’re unlucky. Enjoy the scenery while you can.”

“This place is incredible. No wonder they give you raid access for a full week.”

“I don’t know about that.”

To me, a Gate had long since stopped being a grueling, tedious workplace. It was a place where I could grow even stronger.

“I’m having fun.”

“…Well, I suppose that’s possible.”

Won Myunghoon gave me an odd look, then handed me something.

“Here. Hold on to this.”

“What is it?”

“It has a cold spell enchanted into it, so put it on. You’re an A-Rank, so you’ll be fine for now, but the heat will start draining your Stamina later. You’re one of our main combat assets. You need to conserve your strength.”

“You don’t have to give me something like this, hyung.”

“I’m not giving it to you. I’m lending it to you, so take good care of it and return it later.”

Even at a glance, it looked incredibly expensive.

I hesitated, but Won Myunghoon kept urging me, so I had no choice but to put it on.

Ding.

> **System**
> - You have equipped **Yeti’s Necklace**.
> - A wind from the snowy plains flows from the necklace.

At the same time as the System notification, a chill cold enough to send shivers down my spine wrapped around my entire body.

“It works well.”

“It looks good on you. Keep it on from now on. I need to go deploy the scouting team.”

Won Myunghoon smiled with satisfaction and strode away. The moment his back disappeared from view, I took off the necklace.

*I told him I’m really fine.*

Won Myunghoon might have taken my words for modesty, but I’d only been stating a fact.

When I opened my Conception and Governor Vessels in the Murim, I had gained something far better than *Yeti’s Necklace*.

*Unaffected by Cold and Heat.*

That was why I hadn’t shed a single drop of sweat. It wouldn’t matter if one hour became ten.

This level of heat couldn’t affect me at all.

It would be far better to give the necklace to someone who actually needed it.

“Why are you sweating so much? Are you all right?”

“…Do I look all right?”

“No.”

“Then don’t talk to me. I’m dying here.”

“You should’ve worn something cooler. Team Leader Choi has plenty of magical Equipment.”

“I thought we were going to fight a Manticore, so I went all in on defense. At this rate, they’ll be holding my funeral.”

“We can’t have that. You have a wife and children.”

“Huh? What’s this?”

“A present. Not that I’m giving it to you, of course. I’m only lending it to you while we’re traveling.”

“Whew. I don’t know what this is, but I can finally breathe again.”

—Peeeeep!

I looked up and spotted a dark shape circling impossibly high overhead.

“Wyvern…”

Won Myunghoon had been wrong.

Not half a day. Not a full day.

After only one hour—

It had appeared.
